items.subject: phy
items.q: The error in the measurement of the radius of a sphere is 0.1%. The error in its volume is:
items.explanation: V ∝ R³, so the fractional error in V is three times that in R: 3 × 0.1% = 0.3%.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A body starts falling from height h and travels a distance h/2 during the last second of its motion. The time of flight (in seconds) is:
items.explanation: h = ½gt² and the distance in the first (t − 1) s is h/2, so ½g(t − 1)² = ¼gt². This gives t − 1 = t/√2, so t = √2/(√2 − 1) = 2 + √2 s.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The K.E. of a person is just half the K.E. of a boy whose mass is half that of the person. If the person increases his speed by 1 m/s, his K.E. becomes equal to that of the boy. The initial speed of the person was:
items.explanation: Let the person have mass M and speed u, and the boy speed v. ½Mu² = ½·½(M/2)v² gives v² = 4u². Then ½M(u + 1)² = ½(M/2)v² = Mu², so u + 1 = √2u and u = 1/(√2 − 1) = (√2 + 1) m/s.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Two particles separated by a horizontal distance x are projected towards each other in the same vertical plane: the left one with speed u/√3 at 30° to the horizontal and the right one with speed u at 60° to the horizontal. The time after which the horizontal distance between them becomes zero is:
items.explanation: Horizontal components are (u/√3)cos 30° = u/2 and u cos 60° = u/2, moving towards each other. The relative horizontal speed is u, so the gap x closes in time x/u.

items.subject: phy
items.q: For a particle the displacement–time relation is t = √x + 3. Its displacement when its velocity is zero is:
items.explanation: x = (t − 3)², so v = dx/dt = 2(t − 3). v = 0 at t = 3 s, where x = 0.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A 10 kg block rests on a 40 kg slab, which lies on a smooth floor. The coefficients of friction between block and slab are µs = 0.6 and µk = 0.4. If a horizontal force of 100 N is applied to the 10 kg block, the acceleration produced in the slab is:
items.explanation: Limiting friction is 0.6 × 10 × 9.8 = 58.8 N, which is less than 100 N, so the block slips. The slab is then pulled only by kinetic friction 0.4 × 98 = 39.2 N, so a = 39.2/40 = 0.98 m/s².

items.subject: phy
items.q: Three branches are connected in parallel between two points: (i) an 8 V cell in series with 4 Ω, (ii) an 8 Ω resistor, and (iii) a 6 V cell in series with 6 Ω (both cells have the same polarity). The current in the 8 Ω resistance is:
items.explanation: The two cell branches combine into an equivalent source of emf (8/4 + 6/6)/(1/4 + 1/6) = 7.2 V with internal resistance 2.4 Ω. Current through 8 Ω = 7.2/(2.4 + 8) ≈ 0.69 A.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The effective capacitance of the network between terminals A and B is (four 6 µF capacitors form a bridge, with a 20 µF capacitor across the middle):
items.explanation: All four arms are equal, so the bridge is balanced and the 20 µF capacitor carries no charge. Each arm is two 6 µF in series (3 µF), and the two arms in parallel give 6 µF.

items.subject: phy
items.q: In the circuit, 6 Ω and 4 Ω resistors in series are connected in parallel with a 5 Ω resistor. If the power dissipated in 5 Ω is 20 W, the power dissipated in 4 Ω is:
items.explanation: V²/5 = 20 W gives V = 10 V across the combination. The 6 Ω + 4 Ω branch carries 10/10 = 1 A, so power in 4 Ω = 1² × 4 = 4 W.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A cell of emf E and internal resistance 6 Ω is connected to an external resistance R. The value of R for which the power in it is maximum is:
items.explanation: By the maximum power transfer theorem, power in the load is maximum when the load resistance equals the internal resistance, i.e. R = 6 Ω.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Initially the plane of a coil is parallel to a uniform magnetic field B. In time ∆t it is turned so that its plane is perpendicular to the field. The charge that flows in time ∆t depends on ∆t as:
items.explanation: Induced charge q = (change in flux)/R, which does not involve the time taken. So q is independent of ∆t, i.e. ∝ (∆t)⁰.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A coil of 50 turns and radius 10 cm carries a current of 5 A. The magnetic field at its centre is:

items.subject: phy
items.q: Eight equally charged tiny drops combine to form a big drop. If the potential on each drop is 10 V, the potential of the big drop will be:
items.explanation: Volume conservation gives R = 2r, while the charge becomes 8q. V = kQ/R = k(8q)/(2r) = 4 × 10 V = 40 V.

items.subject: phy
items.q: For an inductor coil L = 0.04 H. The work done by the source to establish a current of 5 A in it is:
items.explanation: The work done against the back emf is stored as magnetic energy, ½LI² = ½ × 0.04 × 5² = 0.5 J. (The original key gives 1.00 J, which does not match ½LI².)

items.subject: phy
items.q: The terminal potential difference of a cell is greater than its emf when:
options: A battery of less emf is connected in its series
A battery of higher emf is connected in its series
A battery of higher emf is connected in its parallel
A battery of less emf is connected in its parallel
items.explanation: V > E only while the cell is being charged, so current is driven into it against its emf. A higher-emf battery connected in parallel does this. (A higher-emf battery in series opposition would also work, so the wording is loose; the key gives the parallel case.)

items.subject: phy
items.q: In Millikan's oil drop experiment a charged drop falls with terminal velocity V. If an electric field E is applied vertically upwards, it moves upward with terminal velocity 2V. If the field is reduced to E/2, its terminal velocity will be:
items.explanation: Viscous drag ∝ velocity: mg = kV and qE − mg = 2kV, so qE = 3kV. With E/2: qE/2 − mg = 1.5kV − kV = 0.5kV, giving an upward terminal velocity V/2.

items.subject: phy
items.q: For a vibration magnetometer, the time period of the suspended bar magnet can be reduced by:
options: Moving it towards the south pole
Moving it towards the north pole
items.explanation: T = 2π√(I/MB_H). The horizontal component B_H of the earth's field is largest at the equator and zero at the poles, so moving towards the equator reduces T.

items.subject: phy
items.q: In the network, inputs A and B each pass through a NOT gate; one AND gate gives ĀB and the other gives AB̄, and these feed an OR gate so that Y = ĀB + AB̄. The truth table (A, B → Y) for the network is:
items.explanation: Y = ĀB + AB̄ is the XOR function. It is 1 only when the inputs differ: 00→0, 01→1, 10→1, 11→0.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A Zener diode is used as:
items.explanation: In reverse breakdown the voltage across a Zener diode stays nearly constant over a wide range of current, so it is used to regulate (stabilise) a d.c. voltage.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The depletion layer of an unbiased p-n junction has:
items.explanation: Electrons and holes near the junction diffuse across and recombine. This leaves behind immobile charged donor and acceptor ions, so the depletion layer contains only static ions.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A cylindrical tube (L = 125 cm) is in resonance with a tuning fork of frequency 330 Hz. If it is being filled with water, the minimum length of water column needed to get resonance again is (v_air = 330 m/s):
items.explanation: λ = 330/330 = 1 m. A closed pipe resonates at air-column lengths λ/4, 3λ/4, 5λ/4 = 25, 75, 125 cm. The next resonance after 125 cm is at 75 cm of air, so the water column is 125 − 75 = 50 cm.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The initial pressure and volume of a gas are P and V. First it is expanded isothermally to 4V, and then compressed adiabatically back to volume V. Its final pressure is (γ = 1.5):
items.explanation: Isothermal: P × V = P₁ × 4V, so P₁ = P/4. Adiabatic: P₂ = (P/4)(4V/V)^1.5 = (P/4) × 8 = 2P.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A sphere at 600 K cools at rate R in surroundings at 200 K. When its temperature falls to 400 K, its cooling rate will be:
items.explanation: By Stefan's law the rate ∝ T⁴ − T₀⁴. Ratio = (400⁴ − 200⁴)/(600⁴ − 200⁴) = (256 − 16)/(1296 − 16) = 240/1280 = 3/16, so the new rate is 3R/16.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A particle is projected with velocity u at angle θ with the horizontal. At the highest point it breaks into two identical parts. If one part retraces its path, the velocity of the other part is:
items.explanation: At the top the velocity is u cos θ. The part retracing its path moves with −u cos θ. Momentum conservation: m u cos θ = (m/2)(−u cos θ) + (m/2)v, so v = 3u cos θ.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The amplitude of a damped oscillator reduces to 1/3 of its initial value in the first 20 s. Its amplitude after the first 40 s becomes:
items.explanation: In damped motion the amplitude falls exponentially, A = A₀e^(−bt). Each 20 s multiplies it by 1/3, so after 40 s it is (1/3)² = 1/9 of the initial value.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Two springs A and B (k_A = 2k_B) are stretched by the same suspended weight. The ratio of work done in stretching A and B is:
items.explanation: With the same force F, W = F²/2k, so W ∝ 1/k. W_A : W_B = k_B : k_A = 1 : 2.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A spring is elongated by length L when a mass M is suspended from it. Now a small extra mass m is attached and the system is released. Its time period of oscillation is:
items.explanation: Spring constant k = Mg/L. The oscillating mass is M + m, so T = 2π√((M + m)/k) = 2π√((M + m)L/Mg).

items.subject: phy
items.q: The frequency of a simple pendulum in a freely falling lift is:
items.explanation: In free fall the effective gravity is zero. Since f = (1/2π)√(g_eff/l), the frequency is zero and the pendulum does not oscillate.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The energy and capacitance of a charged parallel plate capacitor are E and C. A dielectric slab of εr = 6 is inserted, keeping the charge on the plates constant. The energy and capacitance become:
items.explanation: The dielectric multiplies the capacitance by 6, giving 6C. At constant charge, U = Q²/2C, so the energy becomes E/6.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Current conduction in a discharge tube is due to:
items.explanation: The high voltage ionises the gas. Electrons move towards the anode and positive ions towards the cathode, and both carry the current.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Light of amplitude A and wavelength λ is incident on a metal surface whose cut-off wavelength is λ₀. The saturation photocurrent is proportional to:
items.explanation: Emission occurs only if λ < λ₀. The saturation current depends on the number of photons, i.e. on intensity, which is ∝ A².

items.subject: phy
items.q: Light of wavelength 3000 Å gives photoelectrons of maximum K.E. 0.5 eV. If the wavelength is changed to 2000 Å, the maximum K.E. of the emitted electrons will be:
items.explanation: K.E.max = hc/λ − φ. A shorter wavelength means each photon has more energy, so the maximum K.E. increases (by about 2 eV here).

items.subject: phy
items.q: An electron and a photon have the same kinetic energy. The relation between their de Broglie wavelengths is:
items.explanation: For the electron λe = h/√(2mK). For the photon λp = hc/K. λp/λe = √(2mc²/K), which is greater than 1 since K ≪ mc², so λp > λe.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The total energy of an electron is 3.555 MeV. Its kinetic energy is:
items.explanation: Total energy = K.E. + rest energy. The electron's rest energy is about 0.511 MeV, so K.E. ≈ 3.555 − 0.511 ≈ 3.045 MeV.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Two identically charged particles A and B, initially at rest, are accelerated through the same potential difference V. They then enter a transverse uniform magnetic field B and describe circular paths of radii r₁ and r₂. The ratio of their masses is:
items.explanation: r = mv/qB = √(2mqV)/qB, so r ∝ √m for the same q and V. Hence m₁/m₂ = (r₁/r₂)².

items.subject: phy
items.q: A radioactive element emits one α and one β particle. The mass number of the daughter element is:
items.explanation: α emission lowers the mass number by 4. β emission leaves the mass number unchanged, so the net decrease is 4.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The half-life of a radionuclide is 77 days. Its decay constant is:

items.subject: phy
items.q: For a prism of angle A the refractive index is cot(A/2). The angle of minimum deviation is:
items.explanation: µ = sin((A + δ)/2)/sin(A/2) = cos(A/2)/sin(A/2). So sin((A + δ)/2) = cos(A/2) = sin(90° − A/2), giving (A + δ)/2 = 90° − A/2 and δ = 180° − 2A.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Two conducting slabs of equal thickness with thermal conductivities K₁ and K₂ are joined face to face. The outer faces are at temperatures θ₁ and θ₂ (θ₁ > θ₂). The temperature θm of the junction in the steady state is:
items.explanation: In the steady state the same heat current flows through both slabs: K₁(θ₁ − θm) = K₂(θm − θ₂). This gives θm = (K₁θ₁ + K₂θ₂)/(K₁ + K₂).

items.subject: phy
items.q: A particle starts from rest with constant acceleration. The ratio of its space-averaged velocity to its time-averaged velocity is:
items.explanation: Time average = aT/2. Space average = ∫v ds/∫ds = ∫v²dt/∫v dt = (a²T³/3)/(aT²/2) = 2aT/3. Ratio = (2/3)/(1/2) = 4/3.

items.subject: phy
items.q: If the radius of the earth shrinks by 1% (mass remaining the same), then for the acceleration due to gravity:
items.explanation: g = GM/R², so g increases by about 2% everywhere on the surface when R falls by 1%. (This ignores the small effect of the earth's rotation.)

items.subject: phy
items.q: The Rohini satellite is at a height of 500 km and INSAT-B at a height of 3600 km above the earth's surface. The relation between their orbital velocities (V_R, V_I) is:
items.explanation: Orbital speed v = √(GM/r) decreases with orbital radius. Rohini is in the lower orbit, so it moves faster: V_R > V_I.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The mass of the moon is 1/81 of the earth's mass and its diameter is 1/3.7 of the earth's diameter. If g on the earth's surface is 9.8 m/s², its value on the moon is:

items.subject: phy
items.q: When a spring is subjected to a 4 N force its length is a metre, and with a 5 N force its length is b metre. If a 9 N force is applied, its length is:
items.explanation: With natural length l₀: 4 = k(a − l₀) and 5 = k(b − l₀). So k = 1/(b − a) and l₀ = 5a − 4b. Then l = l₀ + 9/k = 5a − 4b + 9(b − a) = 5b − 4a.

items.subject: phy
items.q: For a body the angular velocity is ω⃗ = î − 2ĵ + 3k̂ and the position vector is r⃗ = î + ĵ + k̂. Its velocity is:

items.subject: phy
items.q: A uniform stick of length l = 0.6 m stands vertically on a hinge at its lower end and is released, so that it rotates about the hinge and falls to the ground. The velocity of its free end when it strikes the ground is:
items.explanation: The centre of mass falls by l/2. ½(ml²/3)ω² = mg(l/2) gives ω² = 3g/l, so the tip speed is v = ωl = √(3gl) = √(3 × 9.8 × 0.6) ≈ 4.2 m/s.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The frequency of an electromagnetic wave is 10 MHz. Its wavelength is:

items.subject: phy
items.q: Two particles are projected with the same initial speed, one at angle θ with the horizontal and the other at angle θ with the vertical. If their common range is R, the product of their times of flight is directly proportional to:
items.explanation: t₁ = 2u sin θ/g and t₂ = 2u cos θ/g. So t₁t₂ = 4u² sin θ cos θ/g² = 2R/g, which is ∝ R.

items.subject: phy
items.q: In a compound microscope the magnification is 95. The object is at a distance of 1/3.8 cm from the objective, whose focal length is 1/4 cm. What is the magnification produced by the eyepiece when the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision?
items.explanation: For the objective, 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 4 − 3.8 = 0.2, so v = 5 cm and m₀ = v/u = 5 × 3.8 = 19. Eyepiece magnification = 95/19 = 5.

items.subject: chem
items.q: On the basis of the unit cell concept, crystals are classified into:
items.explanation: Based on the unit cell's axial lengths and angles there are 7 crystal systems. The 14 are Bravais lattices, 32 are point groups and 230 are space groups.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Phenylacetylene reacts with dil. H₂SO₄ in the presence of HgSO₄ to give:
items.explanation: Hg²⁺-catalysed hydration follows Markovnikov's rule. The enol C₆H₅C(OH)=CH₂ tautomerises to acetophenone, C₆H₅COCH₃.

items.subject: chem
items.q: According to the Hardy–Schulze law, the order of coagulating power of the cations will be:
items.explanation: Coagulating power increases sharply with the charge on the oppositely charged ion. So Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following compounds gives p-cresol with p-methylbenzenediazonium chloride?
items.explanation: Warming a diazonium salt with water replaces –N₂⁺ by –OH, so p-CH₃C₆H₄N₂⁺Cl⁻ gives p-cresol. H₃PO₂ would reduce it to toluene, and phenol would couple to form an azo dye.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The mole ratio of H₂ and O₂ gas is 8 : 1. What will be the ratio of their weights?

items.subject: chem
items.q: The ionisation energy of an electron in the second orbit of Li²⁺ will be:

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following electronic configurations will have the maximum difference between the 2nd and 3rd ionisation potentials?
items.explanation: For Mg (3s²) the first two electrons come from the 3s shell. The third must come from the stable neon core, so IE₃ jumps enormously compared with IE₂.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The concentration of a reactant is changed from 0.2 to 0.4. For this first-order reaction with rate constant k = 1 × 10⁻⁶, the rate and rate constant will be:
items.explanation: For first order, rate = k[A] = 1 × 10⁻⁶ × 0.4 = 4 × 10⁻⁷. The rate constant does not depend on concentration, so it stays 1 × 10⁻⁶.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The half-life of a radioactive sample is 4 days. After 16 days, what fraction of the matter remains undecayed?
items.explanation: 16 days is 4 half-lives, so the fraction left is (1/2)⁴ = 1/16.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The structure of trans-2-hexenal is (skeletal structures shown in the figure):
options: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH=CHCHO with the propyl group and CHO on the same side of the C=C
CH₃CH₂CH₂CH=CHCHO with the propyl group and CHO on opposite sides of the C=C
CH₃CH₂CH₂CH=CHCH₂CHO (C=C between C-3 and C-4 of a 7-carbon chain)
items.explanation: Hex-2-enal is CH₃CH₂CH₂CH=CH–CHO. In the trans isomer the propyl group and the CHO group lie on opposite sides of the double bond.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following converts phenyl methyl ketone into ethylbenzene?
items.explanation: Clemmensen reduction (zinc amalgam and conc. HCl) reduces C=O to CH₂, converting C₆H₅COCH₃ into C₆H₅CH₂CH₃. LiAlH₄ would stop at the alcohol.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Acetaldehyde reacts with semicarbazide. The product will be:
items.explanation: In semicarbazide, H₂N–NH–CO–NH₂, the free –NH₂ at the hydrazine end condenses with the C=O group. This gives the semicarbazone CH₃CH=N–NH–CO–NH₂.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The cyanohydrin of which of the following compounds gives an optically active product on hydrolysis?
items.explanation: CH₃CHO gives CH₃CH(OH)CN, which hydrolyses to lactic acid, CH₃CH(OH)COOH, with a chiral carbon. HCHO and acetone give products with no chiral centre. (In practice a racemic mixture forms.)

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following is a chiral compound?
items.explanation: In 2-methylpentanoic acid C-2 carries H, CH₃, COOH and C₃H₇, so it is chiral. 3-methylpentanoic acid is also chiral (C-3 bears H, CH₃, C₂H₅, CH₂COOH), and the original key accepts both (1) and (2). 4-methylpentanoic acid is achiral.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Compound A on chlorination gives compound B. B reacts with alc. KOH to give gas C, which decolourises Baeyer's reagent, and ozonolysis of C gives only HCHO. Compound A is:
items.explanation: An alkene giving only HCHO on ozonolysis is ethene, C. So B is C₂H₅Cl (dehydrohalogenated by alc. KOH), and A is ethane, C₂H₆.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The monomer of natural rubber is:
items.explanation: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene. Its monomer is isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene), CH₂=C(CH₃)–CH=CH₂.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following compounds contains iron in the zero oxidation state?
items.explanation: CO is a neutral ligand, so Fe in Fe(CO)₅ is 0. In the hexacyanoferrates Fe is +2 and +3.

items.subject: chem
items.q: A compound contains C, H and O. If C = 40% and H = 6.67%, the empirical formula of the compound will be:

items.subject: chem
items.q: [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ reacts with excess HNO₃ in water to give:
items.explanation: Excess acid protonates the NH₃ ligands (NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺), so they leave the copper ion. Water molecules take their place, giving the blue aqua complex [Cu(H₂O)₄]²⁺. (The paper prints option 3 garbled; some keys give Cu(NO₃)₂, the salt that would crystallise on evaporation.)

items.subject: chem
items.q: The number of unpaired electrons on Cr in [Cr(NH₃)₆]Br₃ is:
items.explanation: Cr is +3 here, so Cr³⁺ is 3d³. Its three d electrons stay unpaired in t₂g (d²sp³ hybridisation), giving 3 unpaired electrons.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives:
items.explanation: Sucrose hydrolyses to equal amounts of D-(+)-glucose and D-(−)-fructose (invert sugar).

items.subject: chem
items.q: The order of acidic strength of the following compounds will be: (A) p-cresol, (B) phenol, (C) p-nitrophenol, (D) m-nitrophenol
items.explanation: –NO₂ withdraws electrons and stabilises the phenoxide ion, most strongly from the para position (−R and −I) and less from meta (only −I). –CH₃ donates electrons and lowers acidity. So p-nitrophenol > m-nitrophenol > phenol > p-cresol.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following compounds is coloured and has unpaired electrons?
items.explanation: Cu²⁺ (3d⁹) has one unpaired electron and shows d–d transitions, so CuF₂ is coloured and paramagnetic. K₂Cr₂O₇ and KMnO₄ are coloured due to charge transfer but have no unpaired electrons, and low-spin Fe²⁺ in K₄[Fe(CN)₆] is diamagnetic.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following does not reduce Fehling's solution?
items.explanation: In sucrose the glycosidic bond joins the anomeric carbons of both glucose and fructose, so it has no free aldehyde or keto group. It is therefore a non-reducing sugar.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The oxidation number of P in pyrophosphoric acid is:

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following, among BF₃, SnCl₂ and SnCl₄, behave as Lewis acids?
items.explanation: BF₃ has an incomplete octet. SnCl₂ and SnCl₄ can accept electron pairs into vacant orbitals (forming SnCl₃⁻, SnCl₆²⁻). All three are Lewis acids.

items.subject: chem
items.q: In which of the following compounds is a H atom directly linked to phosphorus?
items.explanation: H₃PO₂ (hypophosphorous acid) has two P–H bonds and H₃PO₃ has one, while H₃PO₄ and H₄P₂O₇ have none. The original key accepts both (1) and (2); H₃PO₂ is the best single answer.

items.subject: chem
items.q: In the balanced equation a Zn + b NO₃⁻ + c H⁺ → d NH₄⁺ + e H₂O + f Zn²⁺, the values of a, b, c, d, e and f are:
items.explanation: N goes from +5 to −3 (gain of 8 e⁻) and each Zn loses 2 e⁻, so 4 Zn per NO₃⁻. Balancing H and O gives 4Zn + NO₃⁻ + 10H⁺ → NH₄⁺ + 3H₂O + 4Zn²⁺.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Determine the value of E°cell for the reaction Cu²⁺ + Sn²⁺ → Cu + Sn⁴⁺, whose equilibrium constant is 10⁶:

items.subject: chem
items.q: What will be the H⁺ concentration when 4 g NaOH is dissolved in 1000 mL of water?
items.explanation: 4 g NaOH = 0.1 mol in 1 L, so [OH⁻] = 10⁻¹ M. Then [H⁺] = 10⁻¹⁴/10⁻¹ = 10⁻¹³ M.

items.subject: chem
items.q: What is true for a cyclic process?
items.explanation: Internal energy is a state function, so it returns to its initial value in a cycle and ∆E = 0. ∆H = 0 is also true for the same reason (the original key accepts both (2) and (3)); W need not be zero.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The increasing order of bond length is:
items.explanation: Bond orders are NO⁺ 3, NO 2.5, NO⁻ 2 and O₂⁻ 1.5. Bond length decreases as bond order increases, so NO⁺ < NO < NO⁻ < O₂⁻.

items.subject: chem
items.q: When a system expands adiabatically:
items.explanation: With q = 0, the work done by the expanding system comes from its internal energy. So E decreases (and the temperature falls).

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following is true for a reaction in which all the reactants and products are liquids?
items.explanation: ∆H = ∆E + ∆(PV). For liquids the volume change is negligible (∆n_g = 0), so ∆H ≈ ∆E.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Clemmensen's reaction is:
items.explanation: Clemmensen reduction uses zinc amalgam and conc. HCl to convert C=O into CH₂. Option 2 is the Wolff–Kishner reduction, and option 3 is reduction with HI/red P.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following reactions gives an isocyanide?
items.explanation: In the carbylamine reaction a primary amine is heated with CHCl₃ and alcoholic KOH to give a foul-smelling isocyanide, R–NC.

items.subject: chem
items.q: In a gaseous mixture of NO₂, CO₂ and N₂O, which gases have the same rate of diffusion?
items.explanation: By Graham's law, rate ∝ 1/√M. CO₂ and N₂O both have M = 44, so they diffuse at the same rate. NO₂ has M = 46.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Compound A does not give a precipitate with H₂S in acidic medium but gives a precipitate in NH₄OH medium. Compound A is:
items.explanation: ZnS is too soluble to precipitate at the low S²⁻ level of acidic H₂S (group II). It precipitates as white ZnS in ammoniacal medium (group IV). SnCl₂ gives SnS in acid, and Al³⁺ gives a hydroxide, not a sulphide.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Chromite, FeCr₂O₄, on fusion with Na₂CO₃ (in air) gives the product:
items.explanation: Fusing chromite ore with sodium carbonate in air oxidises Cr(III) to sodium chromate, Na₂CrO₄ (with Fe₂O₃ as by-product). This is the first step in making dichromate. (The paper prints the formula as FeCr₂O₇.)

items.subject: chem
items.q: A compound BA₂ has Ksp = 4 × 10⁻¹². Its solubility will be:
items.explanation: BA₂ ⇌ B²⁺ + 2A⁻, so Ksp = s(2s)² = 4s³. 4s³ = 4 × 10⁻¹² gives s = 10⁻⁴ M.

items.subject: chem
items.q: H₂O₂ on oxidation gives:
items.explanation: When H₂O₂ acts as a reducing agent it is itself oxidised. Oxygen goes from −1 to 0 and O₂ is released: H₂O₂ → O₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻.

items.subject: chem
items.q: What is false for mole fraction?
items.explanation: A mole fraction is a part of a whole, so it always lies between 0 and 1 and can never be negative. The range −2 to 2 is false.

items.subject: chem
items.q: MgO has the same structure as NaCl. In MgO, each magnesium ion is surrounded by how many oxide ions?
items.explanation: In the rock-salt structure each cation sits in an octahedral void, so it is surrounded by 6 anions (6 : 6 coordination).

items.subject: chem
items.q: The general behaviour of O₃ is that it:
items.explanation: Ozone is unstable and readily breaks down as O₃ → O₂ + [O]. The nascent oxygen makes it a strong oxidising agent, so its typical reactions release O₂. (Accepting electrons is also true of an oxidant; the key gives 'gives O₂'.)

items.subject: bio
items.q: How many ATP will be formed by the oxidation of 1 mole of glucose?
items.explanation: In complete aerobic oxidation of one glucose, glycolysis, the link reaction, the Krebs cycle and the ETS give a net 38 ATP by the traditional count. It is 36 in eukaryotes, where 2 ATP are spent shuttling NADH into mitochondria. 36 is the option given.

items.subject: chem
items.q: 400 mL of a gas at 500 torr and 666.6 mL of another gas at 600 torr are put in a 3 L container. The total pressure of the mixture is:
items.explanation: Using P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ for each gas: 500 × 0.4/3 ≈ 66.7 torr and 600 × 0.6666/3 ≈ 133.3 torr. Total ≈ 200 torr.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following is a steroid hormone?
items.explanation: Progesterone is a steroid hormone made from cholesterol. Cholesterol is a steroid but not a hormone, ACTH is a peptide, and adrenaline is an amino-acid (catecholamine) derivative.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The dipole moment of compound AB is 10.92 D and that of CD is 12.45 D. The bond length of AB is 2.72 Å and that of CD is 2.56 Å. Which statement is true for these compounds?
items.explanation: % ionic character = µ_obs/(e × d). For AB: 10.92/(4.8 × 2.72) ≈ 84%. For CD: 12.45/(4.8 × 2.56) ≈ 100%. So CD is more ionic.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Bombardment of ¹⁴₇N with α-particles emits a proton. The new atom will be:
items.explanation: ¹⁴₇N + ⁴₂He → ¹⁷₈O + ¹₁H. Mass number: 14 + 4 − 1 = 17; atomic number: 7 + 2 − 1 = 8.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The half-life of a substance is 77 days. Its decay constant (per day) will be:

items.subject: bio
items.q: The number of base pairs in the human genome (haploid set of chromosomes) is about:
items.explanation: The haploid human genome has about 3 × 10⁹ base pairs (roughly 3.1 billion bp, as found by the Human Genome Project).

items.subject: bio
items.q: The total amount of CO₂ fixed annually by plants is about:
items.explanation: Through photosynthesis the world's plants (land and ocean) fix on the order of 10¹¹ tonnes of carbon dioxide each year. The key gives 7 × 10¹¹ tonnes; estimates vary between textbooks.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The most stable (persistent) pesticides are:
items.explanation: Organochlorines such as DDT, BHC and aldrin are non-biodegradable. They persist for years in soil and tissues and undergo biomagnification. Organophosphates break down much faster.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The most economical method of harvesting solar energy is:
options: Cultivation of sugarcane and obtaining energy by burning it
items.explanation: Energy plantations of fast-growing trees and shrubs trap solar energy cheaply through photosynthesis on otherwise unused land. The biomass can be burnt or converted to fuel.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The main cause of disturbance of biological diversity is:
items.explanation: Habitat loss and fragmentation (deforestation, draining of wetlands, urbanisation) is the single most important cause of species loss.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The best method to preserve the wild relatives of crop plants is:
options: By growing them in their natural habitats
items.explanation: In situ conservation keeps wild relatives in their natural habitats. There they continue to evolve and keep their full genetic variability, which ex situ seed or gene banks cannot fully preserve.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The practical purpose of taxonomy or classification is to:
options: Facilitate the identification of unknown species
items.explanation: The everyday use of classification is to identify organisms. An unknown specimen can be placed in a known group by comparing its characters with keys and descriptions.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Koch's postulates are not applicable to:
items.explanation: Koch's postulates need the pathogen to be grown in pure culture. The leprosy bacillus, Mycobacterium leprae, cannot be cultured on artificial media, so the postulates cannot be satisfied for it.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The amount of DNA in a cell increases during:
items.explanation: At fertilisation two haploid gametes fuse, so the zygote gets double the DNA of each gamete (n + n = 2n). Of the options, only this raises the DNA content of a cell; DNA replication in S phase is not listed.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The initiation codon in eukaryotes is:
items.explanation: AUG (coding for methionine) is the start codon. UGA is a stop codon.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The transition from the exarch bundles of the root to the endarch bundles of the stem occurs in the:
items.explanation: The vascular tissue reorganises from the radial, exarch arrangement of the root to the conjoint, endarch arrangement of the stem in the transition zone. This zone lies in the hypocotyl, between radicle and stem.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which hormone induces the development of the corpus luteum?
items.explanation: The mid-cycle LH surge causes ovulation and converts the ruptured Graafian follicle into the corpus luteum (luteinising hormone).

items.subject: bio
items.q: Plant pathogenic bacteria are mostly:
items.explanation: Most plant pathogenic bacteria (Xanthomonas, Pseudomonas, Erwinia, Agrobacterium) are Gram-negative rods that do not form spores.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The first transgenic plant was:
items.explanation: Tobacco was the first plant to be genetically transformed (1983, with Agrobacterium), as it is easy to regenerate from tissue culture.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Dolly the sheep was obtained by:
options: Cloning: an udder (somatic) cell fused with an enucleated oocyte
items.explanation: Dolly (1996) was produced by somatic cell nuclear transfer. The nucleus of an adult udder cell was fused with an enucleated egg cell, and the embryo was implanted into a surrogate mother.

items.subject: bio
items.q: CCK and secretin are secreted by the:
items.explanation: Cholecystokinin and secretin are secreted by the duodenal mucosa when acidic, fatty chyme enters. They stimulate the pancreas and gall bladder.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Suspensory ligaments are found in the:
items.explanation: The suspensory ligaments (zonule fibres) hold the eye lens and connect it to the ciliary body. They change the lens shape during accommodation.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The life span of a worker honey bee is about:
items.explanation: Worker bees live about 5–6 weeks in the active summer season but several months in winter. The key gives 90 days; the question is dubious since the answer depends on the season.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Parathormone deficiency leads to:
options: Decrease of Ca²⁺ level in blood
Increase of Ca²⁺ level in blood
items.explanation: Parathormone raises blood calcium (from bone, kidney and gut). Its deficiency causes hypocalcaemia, which can lead to tetany.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A gene is composed of:
items.explanation: A gene is a segment of DNA, which is a polynucleotide made of nucleotides (sugar, phosphate and nitrogen base).

items.subject: bio
items.q: Ornithophily (pollination by birds) takes place in:
items.explanation: Bird-pollinated flowers are usually brightly coloured (red, orange or yellow), produce plenty of nectar, and are mostly scentless because birds have a poor sense of smell.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The Bhopal gas tragedy is related to:
items.explanation: In December 1984 methyl isocyanate leaked from the Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, killing thousands of people.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The concentration of DDT is highest in:
items.explanation: DDT is fat-soluble and not excreted, so it builds up at each trophic level (biomagnification). It reaches the highest concentration in top carnivores.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The percentage of energy transferred to the next higher trophic level in a food chain is about:
items.explanation: By Lindeman's 10% law, only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is passed on to the next. The rest is lost mainly as heat in respiration.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What change occurs when one base in DNA is changed?
options: Always a change of one amino acid in the protein
Change in a complex sequence of amino acids
Always a change in the property of the protein
Does not necessarily change the phenotype
items.explanation: Because the code is degenerate, a base substitution may give a codon for the same amino acid (silent mutation), or a similar amino acid with no effect. So the phenotype need not change.

items.subject: bio
items.q: HIV infects:
items.explanation: HIV binds the CD4 receptor and mainly infects and destroys helper T lymphocytes (also macrophages), which cripples the immune system.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following statements is true for bryophytes?
options: Roots provide anchorage to plants along with absorbing water
Gametophyte is dominant and the sporophyte is mostly parasitic
items.explanation: In bryophytes the free-living gametophyte is the main plant body. The sporophyte stays attached to it and depends on it for nutrition (partially or wholly parasitic). They have rhizoids, not true roots.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Lichens can be used as:
options: Bio-indicators of water and air pollution
items.explanation: Lichens are very sensitive to pollutants, especially SO₂, and disappear from polluted areas. They are therefore good bio-indicators of pollution.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Biotic and abiotic components together form a:
items.explanation: Biotic and abiotic components interacting together actually make up an ecosystem, which is not among the options. The key gives community, though a community includes only the living organisms, so the question is flawed.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The endosperm of gymnosperms is:
items.explanation: In gymnosperms the endosperm is the female gametophyte tissue, formed before fertilisation from the haploid megaspore, so it is haploid (n).

items.subject: bio
items.q: The plant having the largest flower is a:
items.explanation: Rafflesia arnoldii has the largest single flower (about 1 m across). It is a total root parasite on Tetrastigma vines.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Anabaena is associated with which part of Azolla?
items.explanation: The nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium Anabaena azollae lives in cavities of the dorsal lobes of Azolla leaves.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The allele for tallness is dominant over that for dwarfness. This is called the:
items.explanation: When one allele of a pair masks the expression of the other in a heterozygote, this is Mendel's law of dominance.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Oxytocin mainly helps in:
items.explanation: Oxytocin causes strong contractions of the uterine smooth muscle during parturition. It also causes milk ejection, but milk production is controlled by prolactin.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What is expected among the offspring if the father is colour blind and the mother's father was colour blind (mother has normal vision)?
items.explanation: The mother is a carrier (XᶜX) and the father is XᶜY. Half the daughters get Xᶜ from both parents and are colour blind; the rest are carriers. Half the sons are colour blind.

items.subject: bio
items.q: When AABBcc is crossed with AaBbCc, the proportion of offspring heterozygous (hybrid) for all three genes is:
items.explanation: Each cross AA × Aa, BB × Bb and cc × Cc gives 1/2 heterozygotes. So the proportion heterozygous for all three is 1/2 × 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/8.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which hormone is concerned with the concentration of urine?
items.explanation: Vasopressin (ADH) increases water reabsorption in the distal and collecting tubules, producing concentrated urine.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Ventricular contraction is under the command of the:
items.explanation: The S.A. node is the pacemaker that starts every heartbeat. Its impulse reaches the ventricles through the A.V. node, bundle of His and Purkinje fibres. The key gives the S.A. node, though the answer depends on whether origin or conduction is meant.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following does not contain a metal?
items.explanation: Ferritin stores iron, cytochromes contain iron in their haem groups, and chromoproteins (e.g. haemoglobin) carry metal-containing pigments. Glycoproteins are protein + carbohydrate with no metal.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A double unit membrane is absent in:
items.explanation: Ribosomes have no membrane at all, while the nucleus and plastids have double membranes. The E.R. has only a single membrane, so it is also a defensible answer; the key gives ribosomes.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The function of nucleases is to:
options: Break the polynucleotide chain by removing each terminal nucleotide
items.explanation: Nucleases hydrolyse the phosphodiester bonds between nucleotides in nucleic acids. Exonucleases act from the ends and endonucleases act within the chain.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What is a phytotron?
options: A device to grow plants in a controlled environment
Growing plants in a green house
A radiation chamber to induce mutations
An apparatus to study the effect of light on plants
items.explanation: A phytotron is a facility where temperature, light, humidity and other factors are precisely controlled. It is used to study plant growth under defined conditions.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Species diversity is maximum in:
items.explanation: Tropical rain forests have warm, stable, wet conditions and high productivity, and support the greatest number of species.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Exponential growth is shown by:
items.explanation: Under ample nutrients, cells in tissue culture divide repeatedly and their number doubles every generation (geometric/exponential growth). Unicellular populations also grow this way, so the question is loose; the key gives cells in tissue culture.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following is a secondary pollutant?
items.explanation: Peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN) is not emitted directly. It forms in photochemical smog from nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons in sunlight. CO, NO₂ and SO₂ are emitted as primary pollutants.

items.subject: bio
items.q: According to the 1997 forest survey report, the total forest cover of India is about:
items.explanation: The State of Forest Report 1997 put India's forest cover at about 19.3% of the geographical area, closest to 19.5%. This is well below the 33% recommended by the National Forest Policy.

items.subject: bio
items.q: During injury, mast cells secrete:
items.explanation: On injury, mast cells release histamine, which dilates blood vessels and increases their permeability, causing inflammation. They also contain heparin, but histamine is the key mediator here.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria convert:
items.explanation: Nitrogenase reduces atmospheric N₂ to ammonia (NH₃). The other conversions are nitrification and denitrification.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Insulin differs from growth hormone in that it:
options: Increases the activity of mRNA and ribosomes
Increases the permeability of the cell membrane
Affects metabolism of fats by inducing lipogenesis
items.explanation: Both hormones promote protein synthesis and uptake processes. Insulin promotes fat synthesis (lipogenesis), whereas growth hormone mobilises fat (lipolysis).

items.subject: bio
items.q: Homologous organs are:
options: Wings of cockroach and wings of bat
Wings of insects and wings of birds
Air bladder of fishes and lungs of frog
Pectoral fins of fishes and forelimbs of horse
items.explanation: Pectoral fins and the forelimbs of a horse share the same basic vertebrate structural plan and origin but do different jobs, so they are homologous. Insect and bird wings are analogous. The air bladder and lungs are also often considered homologous; the key gives option 4.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which arrangement is in the correct ascending order?
items.explanation: The taxonomic hierarchy rises as species → genus → family → order → class → phylum → kingdom.

items.subject: bio
items.q: In the stomach, after physical and chemical digestion, food is called:
items.explanation: Food churned and mixed with gastric juice becomes an acidic semi-fluid called chyme. A bolus is the swallowed mass from the mouth, and chyle is lymph with fat in the lacteals.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The exchange of bicarbonate and chloride ions between RBCs and plasma is called:
items.explanation: HCO₃⁻ made in RBCs diffuses into plasma and Cl⁻ moves in to keep electrical neutrality. This is the chloride (Hamburger) shift.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which gland decreases in size with increasing age?
items.explanation: The thymus is large in children, where it helps T-lymphocytes mature, and it gradually shrinks (involutes) after puberty.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following occurs in maximum concentration in blood plasma (ECF)?
items.explanation: Na⁺ is the main cation of extracellular fluid (about 140 mM). K⁺ is the main intracellular cation.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Large-scale death of fishes occurs in:
items.explanation: In eutrophic lakes, excess nutrients cause algal blooms. Their decomposition uses up dissolved oxygen (high BOD), so fish die of suffocation.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A normal human being requires about how many calories per day?
items.explanation: An average adult doing moderate work needs about 2500 kcal of energy a day. 686 kcal is the energy released by one mole of glucose.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following yields maximum energy?
items.explanation: Aerobic respiration oxidises glucose completely to CO₂ and H₂O, giving about 36–38 ATP per glucose. Glycolysis and anaerobic pathways give only 2 ATP.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The main cause of water blooms in rivers, lakes and seas is:
items.explanation: Water blooms are dense surface growths of cyanobacteria (e.g. Microcystis) in nutrient-rich fresh water and of dinoflagellates (red tides) in the sea.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Insectivorous plants grow in soil that is deficient in:
items.explanation: Insectivorous plants grow in nitrogen-poor soils such as bogs. They trap and digest insects to obtain nitrogen.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which pair consists of insectivorous plants?
items.explanation: Aldrovanda (waterwheel plant) and Utricularia (bladderwort) both trap small animals. Vallisneria and Hydrilla are ordinary aquatic plants, and Rafflesia is a parasite.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What will be the water potential of a root hair cell absorbing water from the soil?
items.explanation: Water moves from higher to lower water potential. The root hair cell has dissolved solutes, so its water potential is negative (less than zero) and lower than that of the soil water.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Deficiency of oxygen affects which organ the most?
items.explanation: Brain cells have a very high oxygen demand and almost no anaerobic reserve. They are damaged within a few minutes of oxygen lack.

items.subject: bio
items.q: DDT is maximum in birds feeding on:
items.explanation: Fish-eating birds (pelicans, ospreys) sit at the top of long aquatic food chains, where DDT is biomagnified most. This causes thin eggshells.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Fully digested food reaches the liver through the:
items.explanation: Absorbed nutrients from the intestine are carried to the liver by the hepatic portal vein. The hepatic artery brings oxygenated blood, and the hepatic vein drains the liver.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Of fraternal twins, one baby is haemophilic while the baby's brother is normal. Which statement is true?
items.explanation: A haemophilic child must get a mutant X from the mother. The normal son got a normal X from her, so the mother must carry one normal and one mutant allele, i.e. she is heterozygous.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following is associated with occupational hazard?
items.explanation: Pneumoconiosis is the general term for lung disease caused by inhaling dust at work (coal, stone, asbestos). Silicosis is one type of it and is also occupational; the key gives pneumoconiosis as the broader term.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Azolla is used as a biofertiliser in the cultivation of:
items.explanation: Azolla, with its nitrogen-fixing partner Anabaena, is grown in flooded paddy fields and adds nitrogen to rice crops.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which organisms produce gas by decomposing cow dung (gobar) in a gobar gas plant?
items.explanation: In the anaerobic digester, methanogenic archaebacteria such as Methanobacterium break down dung to produce methane-rich biogas.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Pantothenic acid and biotin are associated with:
items.explanation: Pantothenic acid (B5) and biotin (B7) are water-soluble members of the vitamin B complex.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which one is a wrong pair?
items.explanation: Beriberi is caused by deficiency of vitamin B1 (thiamine). Vitamin K deficiency affects blood clotting.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Maximum photosynthesis (on earth) is carried out by:
items.explanation: Oceans cover about 70% of the earth's surface. Their phytoplankton (diatoms, dinoflagellates, algae) carry out the major share of global photosynthesis.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Mammal-like reptiles originated in the:
items.explanation: The key gives Triassic, when the first mammals arose from therapsid (mammal-like) reptiles. The therapsids themselves appeared in the Permian, so the wording is dubious.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The dental formula of an adolescent human (below about seventeen years of age, before the wisdom teeth erupt) is:
items.explanation: The adult formula is 2123/2123, but the third molars (wisdom teeth) usually erupt only after about 17 years. Before that the formula is 2122/2122 (28 teeth).

items.subject: bio
items.q: The molecular weight of DNA in yeast is about:
items.explanation: Yeast has a genome of several million base pairs, giving a molecular weight of the order of 10⁹ daltons. The key gives 2.56 × 10⁹; the exact figure varies between sources.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Minute quantities of hormones and steroids are detected by:
items.explanation: Radioimmunoassay uses radiolabelled antigens and specific antibodies to measure hormones at very low (picogram) concentrations.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A hybridoma is:
options: A fusion of a tumour sex cell with a non-tumour sex cell
A fusion of a tumour somatic cell with a non-tumour somatic cell
items.explanation: A hybridoma is made by fusing a myeloma (cancer) cell with an antibody-producing B lymphocyte. It multiplies indefinitely and secretes a single (monoclonal) antibody.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which substance may be used as a male contraceptive in future?
items.explanation: Progestins (often combined with androgen) suppress gonadotropin release and thus sperm production. This has been studied as a hormonal male contraceptive. The key gives progesterone; testosterone-based methods are also being studied, so the question is open to debate.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The genetic material of a prokaryotic cell is:
items.explanation: Bacteria have a naked, circular double-stranded DNA (nucleoid) that is not complexed with histones as eukaryotic chromatin is.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Ligaments consist of:
items.explanation: Ligaments join bone to bone. They are dense connective tissue made of tough collagen (white) fibres along with some elastic (yellow) fibres, which gives them limited stretch.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Tendons consist of:
items.explanation: Tendons join muscle to bone. They are dense regular connective tissue made almost entirely of parallel bundles of collagen (white) fibres, so they are strong and non-elastic.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Industrial melanism is an example of:
items.explanation: In industrial England, soot-darkened trees let dark peppered moths escape bird predation better than light ones. Their frequency rose, which is natural selection in action.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Casparian bands are found in the:
items.explanation: The radial and inner tangential walls of root endodermal cells carry suberin bands (Casparian strips). These block apoplastic water flow into the stele.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The male gametes of Funaria are:
items.explanation: The antherozoids of mosses like Funaria are spirally coiled and biflagellate, and swim through water to reach the archegonium.

items.subject: bio
items.q: E. coli is used in the production of:
items.explanation: Genetically engineered E. coli is used to produce human proteins such as interferon and insulin. Rifampicin comes from Streptomyces/Amycolatopsis.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What was obtained by S. Miller in his 1953 experiment on the origin of life?
items.explanation: Miller passed electric sparks through CH₄, NH₃, H₂ and water vapour in a closed apparatus. Simple organic compounds, notably amino acids, formed.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which protein is found in the maximum amount (on earth)?
items.explanation: RuBisCO, the CO₂-fixing enzyme of the Calvin cycle, makes up a large part of leaf protein. It is the most abundant protein in the biosphere.

items.subject: bio
items.q: After ovulation, the follicle is converted into the:
items.explanation: Under LH, the ruptured Graafian follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone. If there is no pregnancy it degenerates into the corpus albicans.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A minor change in the structure of a gene is called a:
items.explanation: A change in a single base pair (substitution, insertion or deletion) is a point (gene) mutation, e.g. the change causing sickle-cell anaemia.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The greenhouse effect refers to:
items.explanation: Greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄, CFCs, N₂O) trap outgoing infrared radiation. The resulting rise in average global temperature is global warming.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What will happen if the number of organisms increases at a place?
items.explanation: More organisms means more demand for the same limited food and space. Competition then increases both among members of the same species and between different species. The key gives 'both'.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What is a vaccine?
items.explanation: A vaccine is a preparation of killed or weakened pathogens (bacteria or viruses) or their proteins/toxoids. It stimulates active immunity without causing disease.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The eggshells of birds become thin (not properly formed) due to pesticide pollution. This is due to interference with the activity of:
items.explanation: DDT and its breakdown product DDE disturb calcium metabolism in the shell gland, so too little calcium carbonate is deposited. The key gives calmodulin; many sources instead blame inhibition of Ca-ATPase, so this question is debatable.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Agglutination occurs in a blood sample in a test tube. This indicates that:
options: Antibodies are present in the plasma
Antigens are present on the RBCs
Antigens are present in the plasma
Antibodies are present on the RBCs
items.explanation: Agglutination is clumping of red cells when antibodies bind the matching antigens on the RBC surface. It shows that the corresponding antigens are present on the RBCs.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The secondary structure of a protein that spans the lipid layer and lines the pores of the cell membrane will be:
items.explanation: Most transmembrane proteins cross the lipid bilayer as hydrophobic α-helices, and bundles of such helices line membrane channels and pores.

items.subject: bio
items.q: An animal recently extinct from India is:
items.explanation: The Asiatic cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) was declared extinct in India in 1952. Lions, tigers and one-horned rhinos still survive there.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The simplest reflex action in humans is:
items.explanation: The simplest reflex arc, such as the knee-jerk, has just one synapse, between the sensory and the motor neuron.

items.subject: bio
items.q: In an inducible operon, the regulatory gene synthesises:
items.explanation: In an inducible operon such as lac, the regulator (i) gene codes for an active repressor protein. It binds the operator until the inducer inactivates it. An aporepressor belongs to repressible operons.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Neuroglial cells are associated with the:
items.explanation: Neuroglia are the supporting, non-conducting cells of nervous tissue, as in the brain and spinal cord.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Diatomaceous earth is used as a heat insulator in boilers and steam pipes because the cell wall of diatoms is:
items.explanation: Diatom cell walls (frustules) are made of silica (SiO₂). The resulting porous deposit, diatomite, is a poor conductor of heat.
